frozen_decisions.decision: A null total_investment on an otherwise-valid approved SELECTED run is NOT no_run.
frozen_decisions.detail: 'Otherwise valid' means the run has already survived every higher-precedence check: it exists, it has a currently-approved review, it is not legacy_non_authoritative, its currency is USD and its persisted sroi_ratio is not null. no_run is reserved for a project with no selected run at all.

frozen_decisions.decision: A ZERO total_investment on an otherwise-valid approved selected run is NOT no_run.
frozen_decisions.detail: Today a zero investment is neither null nor rejected: it passes toProjectRunSummaryRun unchanged and is summed into the denominator, contributing a zero. That is a different live defect from the null case and it is corrected by the same reason.

frozen_decisions.decision: A NEGATIVE total_investment on an otherwise-valid approved selected run is NOT no_run.
frozen_decisions.detail: Today a negative investment likewise passes the mapper and is summed, and can move the portfolio denominator toward or below zero. Corrected by the same reason.

frozen_decisions.decision: All three cases map to exclusion reason `zero_or_invalid_investment`, evaluated AFTER every higher-precedence exclusion check.
frozen_decisions.detail: The order is the base's EXCLUSION_PRECEDENCE.ordered_list_exact, unchanged and unreordered: no_run, no_approved_run, legacy_non_authoritative, non_usd_currency, no_sroi_ratio, zero_or_invalid_investment. zero_or_invalid_investment is last and is first-match-wins like the other five, so a project that also qualifies for an earlier reason reports the earlier reason and never zero_or_invalid_investment. The set stays closed at six; no seventh reason, no merge, no rename.

frozen_decisions.decision: Changing the expectation and/or the fixture at lib/portfolios/analytics.test.ts:147 as necessary to represent the corrected behaviour is AUTHORIZED, and is NOT weakening of the inherited suite.

PRESERVED_ASSERTIONS_RULE.no_generalization: No future mission may cite this amendment as precedent for editing an inherited assertion. The precedent it sets is narrower than that: where an integrated authority's preservation clause and that same authority's correction requirement are provably unsatisfiable together over one identified assertion, the correction requirement controls for that assertion and the collision must be adjudicated in a governed append-only artifact BEFORE the implementation lands — not asserted by the implementer afterwards.
PRESERVED_ASSERTIONS_RULE.prohibition_restated: Weakening a test or a gate to obtain a PASS remains prohibited. Nothing here creates an exception to that rule; the released assertion is released because the authority requires the behaviour it pins to change, not because it is inconvenient to satisfy.

PARSER_BOUNDARY_RULE.rule: The parser/conversion boundary is PRESERVED and is NOT widened by this amendment. Genuinely unusable or unparseable numeric run data — outside the specific null/zero/negative totalInvestment correction — may still follow the existing parser boundary wherever the base explicitly preserves it.
what_stays: toNumberOrNull (lib/portfolios/analytics.ts:114-118) keeps its contract: a null string stays null, a non-finite parse stays null. It is not made lenient.

The netSocialValue arm of the guard at :136 is untouched by this amendment. A run whose net_social_value is null or unparseable is outside the scope of PF1-MUT-INVESTMENT-1, NEG-AGG-6 and PG-PF1-09, all three of which speak only about total_investment.

The persisted sroi_ratio contract is untouched: NULL stays null, never recomputed as net/investment and never coerced to 0. That is the W2-B3 / AG-B3-2 / FIBC-016 decision pinned at :134-139 and at :107, and the base's own FORMULA and no_sroi_ratio reason depend on it.

The portfolio-level guard at lib/portfolios/analytics.ts:92-94, `totalInvestment.gt(0) ? totalNet.div(totalInvestment).toNumber() : null`, is preserved. It is a different rule from the per-project exclusion: it makes the AGGREGATE ratio null when the summed denominator is not positive. The base's FORMULA.all_excluded_case already says PF1 preserves it, and this amendment does not disturb that.
PARSER_BOUNDARY_RULE.how_the_preserved_intent_may_be_re_hoste: The implementation MAY keep the old parser-boundary test intent alive by moving the fixture at :147 away from the now-corrected totalInvestment case — for example to the independently valid net-value parsing boundary, where a null netSocialValue on an otherwise-valid row still legitimately yields null from toProjectRunSummaryRun — PROVIDED the resulting test truthfully covers the preserved parser contract. 'Truthfully' is the operative word: the moved assertion must exercise a path that really does return null under the corrected implementation. A moved fixture that no longer proves anything, or that proves something the corrected code does not do, is a weakened test and is prohibited by PRESERVED_ASSERTIONS_RULE.
PARSER_BOUNDARY_RULE.boundary_quoted_from_the_base: PF1-MUT-INVESTMENT-1.boundary, verbatim: "This control does not authorize changing what toProjectRunSummaryRun does with a genuinely unparseable numeric column. It requires only that null, zero and negative investment on an otherwise valid selected run be reported as zero_or_invalid_investment." This amendment adopts that boundary word for word and adds nothing to it.
PARSER_BOUNDARY_RULE.consequence_for_the_reason_semantics: zero_or_invalid_investment is a reason about the INVESTMENT FIGURE of a run that otherwise qualifies. It is not a general 'bad row' reason and may not become one. A row that is unusable for a reason other than its total_investment is classified by whichever of the other five reasons applies, or — where the row genuinely does not yield a run at all — by no_run.
